title: Winter fashion sales such as coats, mustangs, and padding are increasing in the middle of summer ami.. - 매일경제
content:
Winter fashion sales such as coats, mustangs, and padding are increasing in the middle of summer amid the continuous heat wave. More and more consumers are trying to buy winter clothes at a time when discounts are high, and the home shopping industry is organizing a variety of special broadcasts from discount events for inventory release to launching new products aimed at demand for new purchases. According to the home shopping industry on the 26th, orders for winter fashion products increased by more than double digits in major companies from June 1 to July 19 this year. GS Shop increased 348% year-on-year, Lotte Home Shopping increased 40% and Hyundai Home Shopping increased 100%. In particular, consumers tended to purchase cashmere coats, mustangs, and wool jackets in advance during the discount period, which are burdened with regular prices. According to GS Shop, coat orders increased 626% year-on-year among winter outerwear, the highest increase. This is attributed to the spread of consumption that prioritizes prices over seasons amid high prices. GS Shop is also targeting demand with the 'warehouse clearance' event, which is the concept of opening a warehouse. The winter fashion discount broadcast was held in the background of the actual distribution center, and the first "SJwani" special recorded 1.4 billion won in orders and 27,000 sales in two hours. Lotte Home Shopping is also raising demand for winter fashion with its special broadcasts. On the 10th, 10,000 sets of "Bybridget" wool jackets were ordered in an hour, and more than 1,000 ramskin goose-down jackets and wool teddy coats of "LBL" were also ordered on the 20th. On the 25th, the company introduced wool jackets, leather jackets, and long boots through its flagship fashion program "L.SHOW." An official from Lotte Home Shopping explained, "In the past, Jian marketing was centered on inventory exhaustion, but recently, it has become a key sales strategy to secure autumn and winter fashion demand in advance." Hyundai Home Shopping is strengthening its "pre-launch" strategy to introduce new winter products first. Since June, it has been targeting demand for new products by unveiling next fall and winter collections of popular brands such as "Riovel," "Diaruche," and "Euro Collection" in advance. title: GS yields jump on inflation fears - BusinessWorld Online
content: YIELDS on government securities (GS) traded in the secondary market ended mostly higher last week as investors priced in heightened inflation risks from surging global oil prices and the peso’s slide to a fresh record low. GS yields, which move opposite to prices, climbed by an average of 19.98 basis points (bps) week on week, based on the PHP Bloomberg Valuation Service Reference Rates as of July 24 published on the Philippine Dealing System’s website. At the short end of the curve, yields were mixed. Rates of the 182- and 364-day Treasury bills (T-bills) dropped by 5.1 bps to 5.4814% and 1.15 bps to 5.9696%, respectively. On the other hand, the 91-day tenor inched up by 0.27 bp to yield 5.0628%. Meanwhile, yields at the belly and long end climbed across the board week on week. Rates of the two-, three-, four-, five-, and seven-year Treasury bonds (T-bonds) rose by 16.87 bps (to 6.7234%), 21.52 bps (7.0351%), 24.99 bps (7.2639%), 25.55 bps (7.4015%), and 24.38 bps (7.5446%), respectively. The 10-, 20-, and 25-year tenors increased by 32.24 bps, 40.29 bps, and 39.92 bps to yield 7.6050%, 7.4354%, and 7.4315%, respectively. GS volume traded reached P22.93 billion on Friday, slightly lower than the P23.49 billion logged a week earlier. “The market was driven by higher inflation expectations as global oil prices jumped following the escalation in US-Iran tensions,” the first bond trader said in a Viber message. The second trader said the peso’s slide and elevated crude oil prices revived concerns about domestic inflation. The trader added that military skirmishes in the Strait of Hormuz and the closure of the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait by Houthi rebels have “effectively choked the passage of oil exports from the Arabian Peninsula.” The Philippine peso closed at a new all-time low of P61.847 per dollar on Friday as escalating conflict in the Middle East pushed Brent crude oil prices back above $100 a barrel. The local unit also fell to as low as P61.85 against the greenback during intraday trading, surpassing the previous record of P61.75 first hit on April 30. The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) expects headline inflation to remain above its 3% point target through 2028, with forecasts of 6.4% in 2026, 4.5% in 2027, and 3.1% in 2028. Headline inflation has exceeded the BSP’s 2%-4% tolerance band since March amid the energy price shock caused by the Middle East conflict. In June, inflation eased to 6.4% from 6.8% in May as oil prices retreated following an interim peace agreement between the United States and Iran. For the first half, headline inflation averaged 4.8%. Core inflation, however, accelerated for a sixth straight month to 4.4% in June, its fastest pace in nearly three years. For this week, both traders said the market will track inflation-related data and geopolitical developments for fresh direction. “[This] week’s report on the Fed’s inflation gauge… will be monitored whether this report will be sufficient to allow the US central bank to consider rate hikes a bit later this year,” the second trader said. A possible diplomatic breakthrough in the Middle East could help ease supply concerns and temper oil price pressures, the trader said. The first trader added the Bureau of the Treasury’s higher borrowing program for this quarter could exert upward pressure on yields as increased supply would require stronger investor demand.

title: The Adventure Bike That Can Replace Almost Everything In Your Garage - Top Speed
content: If you’ve been blessed enough to have a garage full of motorcycles, then chances are that it looks something like this. A sport bike stands under a cover in the corner, ridden just twice since spring, because hitting the track requires an interstate journey, but touring isn’t its forte. A dirt bike lies behind it with flat tires and a battery tethered to a trickle charger. Parked out front is the tourer that has been doing the daily grind. Three bikes, barely enough time to maintain all of them, piling expenses, and only one of them that hits the road with some regularity. That’s a hard-to-admit reality of one person with multiple bikes. Trouble is, none of those three bikes could cover the other two. They are all specialized products for a given use case, and anything outside of that is a compromise that, at the very least, is annoying, and at best, is avoided. A genuine do-everything machine, then, has to clear a higher bar than any one of those three individually. It needs enough chassis composure and power delivery to feel legitimately quick on a road that rewards commitment. At the same time, it has to offer enough wind protection and ergonomic range to make hours between fuel stops feel routine rather than punishing. A middleweight ADV is a great solution to replace two or more bikes, but you might crave the power deficit it has against the sport bike. While there’s also the need for enough ground clearance and suspension travel to survive loose surfaces. Very few bikes meet these criteria. Fewer still do it without feeling like a compromise stacked on a compromise. BMW built the R 80 G/S in 1980 on the idea that one motorcycle could genuinely go anywhere, and the latest R 1300 GS pushes that idea further than any generation before it. The 1,300cc boxer-twin sits low in a two-part frame that uses the engine itself as a stressed member, a layout BMW has used since the platform's earliest days to keep weight centered. At $20,395, it costs more than a sport bike and a dirt bike combined in some cases, but it’s also the very point that it’s trying to make: that it might be the only bike a rider needs to buy for a long time to come. Every R 1300 GS has four riding modes as standard in the form of Eco, Rain, Road, and Enduro, each recalibrating throttle response and traction control for a different kind of day in the saddle. The optional Dynamics package adds Shift Assistant Pro for clutchless gear changes, Dynamic Suspension Adjustment (DSA), a sportier brake setup, and a pair of Pro riding modes that push the same chassis toward opposite ends of what one motorcycle can be asked to do. One setting dials in for the canyon road. Another tackles the washed-out fire road. So true do-it-all capabilities in an ADV with optional extras that still cost less than some of its competitors. You could decide to throw everything at the big GS, and it’ll handle it with aplomb. Switch into Dynamic or Dynamic Pro, and the throttle mapping sharpens, delivering power right off the lightest twist of the wrist instead of easing into it the way Road mode does. Shift Assistant Pro, part of the same Dynamics package, lets the rider go up and down the gearbox without ever touching the clutch lever. So transitioning from the urban environment to a set of twisties is a fluid change from convenience to excitement. The optional DSA suspension firms up damping on the fly as lean angle and speed climb, holding the chassis flatter under hard braking into a bend than the standard setup. None of it turns a 523-pound adventure bike into a proper sport bike, but it closes the gap substantially. Enduro mode alone, standard on every R 1300 GS, already loosens the electronics' grip on loose surfaces, letting the rear step out a little without traction control slamming the door shut on it. Enduro Pro, unlocked through the same Dynamics package, goes further still. Tuned around aggressive knobby rubber, it dials back electronic intervention enough that a rider can power the bike through sand or loose rock on throttle input rather than on what the electronics allow. Riders chasing serious trail use can also swap the standard cast wheels for optional forged enduro wheels, shaving weight in the unsprung mass spinning at each end of the bike. It’s truly the most durable ADV for America. The R 1300 GS’ versatile range continues to hold up away from a canyon or a trail as well, and it’s exactly why it gets the respect that it does for catering to all kinds of riding duties. The standard seat sits at 33.4 inches, but optional low and high comfort seats swing that range from 31.5 to 35 inches, so the R 1300 GS fits a range of riders. Heated grips and a Tire Pressure Monitor come standard, and so does a sport windscreen that adjusts by hand for better wind protection at highway speed. Radar-based guidance backs the optional Active Cruise Control that holds a set following distance in traffic or on a long interstate stretch, cutting fatigue on both kinds of ride. Add the optional Vario luggage system and the same bike can carry a week of gear for the tour. None of this versatility matters if the engine underneath it can't rack up the miles to prove it. The liquid-cooled 1,300cc ShiftCam boxer-twin features double overhead cams and BMW's variable valve timing, filling out the power curve to 145 hp and 110 lb-ft through a six-speed gearbox and a shaft final drive. While previously infamous for reliability issues, BMW has come a long way to bust those myths. The shaft drive is the first reliability win on its own, since it skips the sprockets, chain lube, and midlife replacement a chain-driven system eventually requires. BMW also spaces oil change intervals at 6,000 miles and valve clearance checks at 12,000, a decently long interval to keep things refreshed after your continent-crossing antics are done. The boxer's cylinder heads sit out in open air on either side of the bike rather than buried under bodywork, so cooling and access both work in the engine's favor over a long ownership run. It’s also one of the reasons that the big GS actually costs less to own and maintain. None of that guarantees a trouble-free bike on its own, but it's a proven assimilation of parts and engineering that has carried generations of GS owners past six figures on the odometer, and there's no reason to expect this one to break that streak. The R 1300 GS’ closest rivals don’t seem to win outright. The Ducati Multistrada V4 undercuts it on price, is more powerful at 170 horsepower, but riding on 19-inch cast wheels hints at its road-to-light-trails focus rather than a complete all-round build. The KTM 1390 Super Adventure R swings the other way entirely, priced higher at $21,649 with a proper 21-inch spoked front wheel, and 9.45 inches of suspension travel at each end, tipping the scales more towards off-road terrain. While the 1390 Super Adventure S is nearly as road-focused as a road and track weapon. Neither rival is a huge compromise, as the inherent traits of an adventure-tourer remain intact and lots of versatility is built in by default. The Ducati is the sharper road bike; the KTM is an either-or situation, given the trims. But the GS is neither the fastest nor the most extreme of the three, but it's the only one that doesn't ever demand a rider to give up an entire category of riding. title: GS Retail Arranges Program for Rainbow Box Orchestra Members to Join Pyeongchang Daegwallyeong Music Festival - 스포츠조선

By
																						
												SoHyung, Kim Members of the Rainbow Box Orchestra, sponsored by GS Retail, took part in the Pyeongchang Daegwallyeong Music Festival. The Pyeongchang Daegwallyeong Music Festival, a classical music event held in Pyeongchang, Gangwon State, is marking its 23rd edition this year. Under the theme of "Inheritance and Innovation," it opened on July 23 and runs through Aug. 2 across Pyeongchang, Gangwon State. The festival will feature a range of performances, including chamber music, solo recitals and orchestral concerts. It will also offer side events such as coffee and wine academies with artists. Rainbow Box, GS Retail's flagship cultural social contribution program, has been run since 2005 with Hope Friend Hunger Countermeasures. Now in its 21st year, the program has accumulated 5.45 billion won in donations and has supported instrument education and ensemble activities for more than 13,000 children at 755 local children's centers nationwide, helping them build emotional stability and develop artistic talent. GS Retail, which began sponsoring the Pyeongchang Daegwallyeong Music Festival in 2024, has expanded artistic experiences for Rainbow Box members through its collaboration with the Gangwon Art & Culture Foundation. This year, the company organized a two-day, one-night program for 26 participants, including Rainbow Box Orchestra members and instructors. They attended performances and a special lecture by mathematician Minhyong Kim, spending time experiencing classical music and a variety of arts and culture firsthand. Park Kyung-rang, head of the ESG team in GS Retail's policy support division, said, "We will continue our ESG activities so that Rainbow Box members can keep growing their dreams through diverse cultural experiences." title: How Many G's Do F1 Drivers Experience? 2026 F1 G-Force Data - Yahoo Sports
content: F1 drivers experience roughly 2 to 3G during normal 2026 racing laps, with braking events averaging 2.0 to 2.3G across the heaviest stops of the season. Spa produced the hardest braking zone measured so far, at 2.34G. The 2026 cars generate lower peaks than the 6G-plus figures quoted for the previous generation, because they run lighter and carry less downforce. Normal racing produces roughly 2 to 3G through most corners and straights. The hardest braking zone of the 2026 season sits at Spa, averaging 2.34G from 275 km/h to 93 km/h in 2.08 seconds. The softest braking zone among the nine circuits measured is Silverstone, at 1.78G. Standing-start acceleration averages 1.0G from 0-100 km/h and 1.4G from 100-200 km/h. The highest confirmed g-force in a modern F1 crash is 67G, from Romain Grosjean’s 2020 Bahrain accident. The 2026 cars run a minimum weight of 768kg, about 30kg lighter than the previous generation, with roughly 30 percent less downforce in cornering trim. Spa-Francorchamps produced the hardest braking of the 2026 season so far. The top five qualifiers there averaged 2.34G through the entire braking zone into the Bus Stop chicane, slowing from 275 km/h to 93 km/h in 2.08 seconds. Every figure in that graphic comes from F1 Chronicle’s analysis of official F1 timing data for the 2026 season: the median deceleration across the full braking zone for the top five qualifiers at each round, taken from dry sessions across rounds one to ten. That whole-zone average is a deliberate choice, and it explains why these numbers read lower than the peak figures quoted elsewhere. Instantaneous peak deceleration spikes higher for a fraction of a second at the sharpest point of a stop, but qualifying telemetry of this kind cannot responsibly be used to claim a specific peak. The averages here are lower because they measure something different, not because they are less accurate. G-force measures acceleration against the pull of gravity. One G equals the force a stationary body feels at rest on Earth; braking, cornering or accelerating at 2G means the body is being pushed with twice its own weight. A road car braking hard at a red light pulls about 1G. An F1 car under braking pulls more than double that. F1 generates such high g-force because of downforce. The front and rear wings, floor and diffuser press the car onto the track at speed, which lets the tyres generate far more grip than a road car’s. More grip means the car can brake later, corner faster and accelerate harder, and every one of those forces registers as g on the driver’s body and neck. Belgian Grand Prix standing-start telemetry from the top five finishers shows a 2026 car accelerating at 1.0G on average from 0-100 km/h, rising to 1.4G from 100-200 km/h. That climb is the counterintuitive part. A road car’s hardest acceleration comes off the line, when the engine’s torque advantage is greatest and there is nothing left to give as speed builds. An F1 car does the opposite. Downforce grows with speed, and grip grows with it, so a 2026 car accelerates harder at 150 km/h than it does leaving the grid, even though the engine produces roughly the same power throughout. F1 Chronicle’s breakdown of how much horsepower an F1 car has covers where that power comes from; this is what the car does with it once the tyres have grip to use. Spa sits at the top of the list at 2.34G, with Suzuka close behind at 2.22G and Shanghai at 2.18G. Miami (2.17G), Monaco (2.11G) and the Red Bull Ring (2.06G) fill the middle of the field, followed by Barcelona at 2.04G and Melbourne at 1.95G. Silverstone produced the gentlest of the nine measured stops, at 1.78G, for its biggest braking zone of the lap. Even Monaco, the slowest circuit on the calendar by average lap speed, produces a serious braking event: cars arrive at the chicane out of the tunnel at 282 km/h and shed most of that in a 2.11G stop. Canada does not appear on this list. That weekend fell outside the dry-session criteria this analysis uses, after rain affected track conditions. The 2026 cars are lighter and carry less downforce than the generation they replaced, and both changes show up directly in the g-force numbers. The minimum weight for 2026 is 768kg, about 30kg lighter than under the previous regulations. Cornering downforce, in the cars’ highest-downforce Z-mode setting, runs roughly 30 percent below the best 2025-specification cars. The 2026 regulations also introduced active aerodynamics, with drivers switching the wings between a low-drag setting on straights and a high-downforce setting through corners, so the load on the car, and on the driver, changes constantly through a single lap rather than sitting at one fixed level. None of this makes the figures quoted for 2022-2025 cars wrong. Those cars were heavier, ran more downforce, and produced the higher peak numbers still repeated across the web. They are describing a car that no longer exists on the grid. Race conditions push the numbers lower again. Drivers brake earlier and softer in the race than they do in qualifying, easing off sooner to harvest energy for the hybrid system rather than attacking the limit on every lap. F1 Chronicle’s Belgian Grand Prix telemetry analysis measured lift-and-coast beginning around 50 metres earlier in the race than in qualifying across the lap’s braking zones, one of the reasons the g-force a driver feels on Sunday sits below even the qualifying averages used in this analysis. Crash forces sit in a different category from racing g. They are a single violent spike rather than a sustained load, and the highest figures on record dwarf anything a driver feels in normal use of the car. Romain Grosjean’s fireball crash at the 2020 Bahrain Grand Prix remains the highest confirmed figure in modern F1. The FIA’s investigation into the accident found Grosjean experienced a peak of 67G when his car struck the barrier. Max Verstappen’s high-speed crash at the 2021 British Grand Prix, after contact with Lewis Hamilton on the opening lap, registered 51G. Further back, David Purley survived an estimated 179.8G in a 1977 crash at Silverstone, decelerating from 173 km/h to a complete stop in just 66 centimetres after his throttle stuck open, among the highest g-loads a person has ever survived in a recorded incident. Jules Bianchi’s fatal crash at the 2014 Japanese Grand Prix has no official g-force figure attached to it. The FIA’s ten-person accident panel found instead that his car struck a 6,500kg recovery vehicle at around 126 km/h, an impact so severe the panel concluded no realistic safety structure could have prevented what it called non-survivable decelerations. These numbers explain why F1 keeps investing in cockpit safety even as racing g stays flat or falls. A car only needs to protect a driver from 2 to 3G for 300 kilometres of racing. It has to protect them from more than 60G in the fraction of a second when everything goes wrong. Neck and core strength are non-negotiable for an F1 driver, because sustained cornering and braking repeatedly pulls the head and helmet sideways and forward for the length of a race. Drivers build that strength through rowing, cable work and isometric neck training, alongside the cardio base needed to keep those muscles firing deep into a two-hour race. Many teams also use G-force simulators and centrifuge-style rigs so drivers get used to the physical sensation of sustained lateral load before they ever feel it in the car. The HANS device, short for head and neck support, is the piece of safety equipment that makes the sport’s crash forces survivable at all. It secures the helmet to a collar worn around the driver’s shoulders, so that in an impact the head is restrained rather than snapping forward on the neck alone. Every driver on the 2026 grid wears one, a direct response to exactly the kind of forces measured in the Grosjean and Purley crashes above. Want more F1Chronicle.com coverage? title: Karol G’s Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour Is a Bold, Joyous Ode to Latina Power - Rolling Stone
content: There are many artists having what could easily be considered a “good run.” And then there’s Karol G, who kicked off her latest headlining stadium tour — Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour — with the first of two sold-out nights at Chicago’s Soldier Field on Friday. Loosen your hips, cue the fireworks, pyro, and ready the giant guacamaya. No for real, she sings atop one. The Colombian singer has continued to define new heights for herself since winning Best New Artist at the Latin Grammys in 2018. Nearly a decade into her career, she made history repeatedly: She’s become the first Latina artist to [insert incredible achievement in pop music here], from becoming the first female artist to reach number one on the Billboard 200 chart with a primarily Spanish-language album to headlining Coachella to holding 11 Guinness World Records for her record-breaking streaming numbers, tour sales and other milestones. She’s captained a handful of back-to-back international, headlining tours in the past five years – all preparing her for this, her largest, most intentional procession yet. The opening show at Soldier Field kicked off a trek that’ll take her to 63 stadiums across North and Latin America, as well as Europe through mid-2027. For just under two and a half hours, after an opening set from Elena Rose, Karol and her troupe of no less than 20 dancers delivered a proud, ambitious and emotional production on a massive stage reimagined as the Colombian mountainside and rainforest that magnified her historic Coachella outing. Her multilevel “cave club” came alive through four acts telling the story of a woman reborn and buoyed on a mission of self-discovery by her ancestors and the land. The scene at Soldier Field was awash in the colors of the sunset: bright oranges, exuberant pinks, glittering golds and huge floral prints. An intergenerational fanbase from all over the Latin American diaspora, folks arrived in their dancing shoes (for which, seemingly, no heel was too high for the occasion or walk across Museum Campus) and outfits that ranged from their country’s flags fashioned as skirts to recreations of the artist’s feathered sunglasses by Chrishabana. A celebration of, not only Karol’s influence but cultura that binds millions, she opened her set with “Latina Foreva” in a fierce declaration of the evening’s agenda, before rolling right along into favorites including “Un Gatito Me Llamo,” “Qlona” and “El Makinon.” It felt almost ironic that her tour would start the week when United States congressmen debated the meaning of “Latina power” in a House subcommittee meeting. If you needed a lesson, Karol came equipped. As Act II was introduced by a pre-recorded vignette featuring famed Mexican-American actor Edward James Olmos, both he and Karol spoke passionately about the commitment to family, friends, work, ritual and joy. Later, an all-female mariachi troupe joined for a handful of songs including the traditional “Negrita de Mis Pesares,” plus Karol’s hits “Ese Hombre Es Malo,” “Mamiii” (which she made into a global smash with Becky G),” and “200 Copas.” There were also indelible fan interactions, like a lucky couple who was promised tickets to another Karol concert in Paris for their honeymoon. One thing was clear: being a tropicoqueta runs deep. Sure, some transitions were a bit clunky. At one point attendees questioned if the electricity went out, but a few moments of silence quickly gave way to thumping congas, horns, and wood flutes from a live band that only seemed to grow as they played cumbias and porros. As dancers writhed and contorted themselves in an elongated sequence that took over a satellite stage disguised as a lagoon (ticketholders, you may be in the splash zone just FYI) and a DJ spun additional hits like “A Ella” and “Provenza,” Karol readied herself for the final act. Dressed head-to-toe in bejeweled orchids, she addressed and thanked her audience again. “Being Latino is the coolest thing in the world,” Karol said in Spanish to uproarious applause, before adding that life is really about the simple things. She flexed unexpected vocal acrobatics on “Si Antes Te Hubiera Conocido” and “Viajando Por El Mundo” to bring it all home. As dancers ran across the stage carrying kites and flags of all the countries in the Americas, confetti fell from cannons onto the crowd. At the end, she debuted her new single, “Matadora.” Confident, strong, sexy, secure, full of heart, Karol showed that being a “bichota” and “tropicoqueta” is a global movement. Find your own guacamaya and get on board. title: Is Goldman Sachs (GS) Primed for a Q1 Earnings Beat - Kavout | AI
content: Goldman Sachs (NYSE:GS) is set to announce its first-quarter 2026 earnings before market open on Monday, April 13, 2026, and Wall Street is bracing for a robust performance. The investment banking giant has a history of exceeding expectations, with an impressive average earnings surprise of 14.02% over the last four quarters. This consistent outperformance sets a high bar, yet current market dynamics suggest the firm is well-positioned to clear it once again. Analysts are forecasting a significant uplift, with consensus estimates for Q1 2026 revenue ranging from $16.66 billion to $17.40 billion, representing a projected 12.9% year-over-year increase. Earnings per share (EPS) are anticipated to be in the range of $16.41 to $16.86. These figures underscore a period of strong client activity and market volatility that Goldman Sachs has historically capitalized on, particularly within its Global Banking & Markets division. The current market environment, characterized by shifting expectations around artificial intelligence, persistent inflation concerns, and geopolitical tensions, has fueled volatility across asset classes. This backdrop creates fertile ground for Goldman's market-making and trading desks. While the broader M&A landscape remains somewhat subdued, the resurgence in initial public offerings (IPOs) and strong bond issuance volumes are expected to provide a significant tailwind to investment banking fees. However, it's not all smooth sailing. Goldman faces rising operating expenses due to ongoing investments in technology and strategic growth initiatives. The firm's ability to manage these costs while delivering top-line growth will be a critical focus for investors. Despite these headwinds, the overall sentiment remains cautiously optimistic, with the firm's strategic realignment towards a more diversified revenue base proving effective in a fractured global economy. Goldman Sachs' Q1 performance will largely hinge on the strength of its core operating segments, particularly Global Banking & Markets. This division, encompassing investment banking, equities, and fixed income, currencies, and commodities (FICC) trading, is expected to be the primary engine of revenue growth. Analysts project 'Net Revenues - Global Banking & Markets - Total' to reach approximately $12.65 billion, marking an 18.1% increase from the prior-year quarter. Within this segment, trading desks are anticipated to deliver exceptional results. High market volatility across equities, commodities, bonds, and foreign exchange, coupled with robust client activity, has created favorable conditions. In Q4 2025, the firm reported record equity trading revenue of $4.31 billion and a 12.5% rise in FICC revenue to $3.11 billion, and this momentum is expected to have carried into Q1 2026. The ability to monetize volatility remains a hallmark of Goldman's trading prowess. Investment Banking (IB) fees are also projected to see a substantial rebound, with consensus estimates at $2.6 billion, a 33.1% rise year-over-year. This resurgence is primarily driven by an impressive IPO market and solid global bond issuance volumes. While the M&A engine has sputtered due to regulatory scrutiny and geopolitical uncertainty, Goldman's leadership in equity capital markets and advisory services for strategic transformation deals has helped offset some of the broader slowdown. However, the stalling M&A landscape remains an "elephant in the room." While a handful of "megadeals" in technology and energy have kept some activity afloat, broader mid-market volume has plummeted. This creates pressure for Goldman to demonstrate the resilience of its fee-based revenue model even when one of its primary engines is idling. The firm's strategic pivot towards capital-light, fee-generating activities like IPO underwriting, rather than capital-intensive bridge financing for M&A, is a direct response to evolving market and regulatory conditions. Goldman Sachs' current valuation metrics present a mixed picture, reflecting both its strong operational performance and the inherent risks of the financial sector. The stock is currently trading at $907.80, with a market capitalization of $269.39 billion. Its trailing twelve-month (TTM) P/E ratio stands at 16.53, which is slightly above the industry average of 15.13x but below its 52-week high of $984.70. This suggests the market is pricing in continued growth, but perhaps with some caution. The price-to-book (P/B) ratio of 2.27 indicates that the market values Goldman Sachs at more than twice its book value per share of $399.65. While this can be a sign of strong asset quality and brand equity, it also highlights that the stock is not trading at a deep discount. The firm's debt-to-equity ratio of 4.88 is a point of consideration, reflecting the highly leveraged nature of investment banking, though this is typical for large financial institutions. Analyst sentiment for GS is generally positive, albeit with a "Hold" consensus rating from 55 analysts. Out of these, 22 recommend a "Buy," 30 suggest a "Hold," and only 3 advise "Sell." The median price target is $990.00, implying an upside of approximately 9% from the current price, with a high target of $1100.00. Recent rating changes from Evercore ISI Group and Jefferies both maintained "Outperform" and "Buy" ratings, respectively, on April 6, 2026, just days before the earnings release. Despite the positive outlook from many analysts, the stock's performance in Q1 2026 saw Goldman's shares lose 3.7%, while the broader industry declined by 8.6%. This relative outperformance, even in a down quarter, underscores the firm's resilience. However, the slight downward revision of 3.7% in the consensus EPS estimate over the past 30 days suggests some analysts have tempered their initial projections, making the actual earnings beat even more critical for investor confidence. The bull case for Goldman Sachs post-earnings hinges on several powerful tailwinds. First, the firm's ability to consistently beat earnings estimates, with an average surprise of 14.02%, suggests a strong operational execution that often exceeds conservative analyst models. If Q1 2026 continues this trend, it could provide a significant boost to investor confidence and the stock price. The projected 12.9% year-over-year revenue increase, driven by robust trading and ECM, indicates strong underlying business momentum. Furthermore, Goldman's strategic pivot towards a more diversified, fee-based revenue model, emphasizing Asset & Wealth Management, offers a more stable earnings base less susceptible to the boom-and-bust cycles of traditional investment banking. The firm's asset turnover of 0.07 and return on equity (ROE) of 13.8% demonstrate efficient capital deployment and strong profitability. Should geopolitical tensions de-escalate in the latter half of 2026, a massive backlog of "paused" M&A deals could unleash a record-breaking period, with Goldman perfectly positioned to capture this "snap-back" activity given its #1 ranking in deal volume. However, the bear case presents equally compelling arguments. The stalling M&A engine, a traditional stronghold for Goldman, remains a significant headwind. Regulatory scrutiny, particularly on "megadeals" in defense and energy, is causing "regulatory friction" and delaying transactions, forcing corporate boards to prioritize organic growth over acquisitions. This shift fundamentally alters the Wall Street landscape, and while Goldman is adapting, the long-term impact on its advisory revenue stream is uncertain. Rising operating expenses, fueled by investments in technology and growth initiatives, could compress margins if revenue growth doesn't keep pace. The firm's current ratio of 0.83 indicates a less liquid position than some peers, and its net debt/EBITDA of 18.53 highlights a substantial debt load relative to earnings. Moreover, insider trading activity shows a clear trend of net selling, with 133 sales and 0 purchases over the past 6 months, including significant sales from EVP John F.W. Rogers and CFO Denis P. Coleman totaling roughly $112 million. This insider behavior could signal a lack of conviction in the stock's near-term upside, despite the positive analyst outlook. For investors, Goldman Sachs' upcoming Q1 2026 earnings report represents a crucial inflection point. The firm's ability to navigate a complex macroeconomic environment, characterized by both high volatility and regulatory headwinds, will be under intense scrutiny. A strong beat, particularly in its Global Banking & Markets and Asset & Wealth Management divisions, could reinforce the narrative of a resilient, adaptable financial powerhouse. The market is currently pricing in a decent performance, but any significant deviation from analyst expectations could trigger a sharp reaction. Investors should pay close attention to management's commentary on the outlook for M&A activity, the sustainability of trading volumes, and the trajectory of operating expenses. The strategic pivot towards wealth and asset management, alongside its robust trading operations, is key to Goldman's long-term "durability" and less dependence on the cyclical nature of investment banking. Goldman's dividend yield of 1.80% and quarterly payout of $4.50 per share, with a payout ratio of 30.7%, offers a steady income stream, but capital appreciation will depend heavily on its ability to execute its strategy and capitalize on market opportunities. The firm's forward estimates for FY 2028 and FY 2029 revenue of $68.1 billion and $69.0 billion, respectively, and EPS of $71.36 and $75.79, suggest a positive long-term growth trajectory. Ultimately, Goldman Sachs remains a bellwether for the broader financial industry. Its Q1 results will not only reflect its own performance but also offer insights into the health of capital markets and the global economy. Investors should approach the earnings call with a balanced perspective, weighing the firm's proven ability to monetize volatility against the persistent challenges in certain core segments. Goldman Sachs is demonstrating remarkable resilience, leveraging its dominance in trading and capital markets to offset M&A headwinds. The upcoming earnings report will be a critical test of its strategic adaptability and ability to deliver value in a high-stakes environment. The Colombian megastar kicked off the concert with her anthem “LATINA FOREVA.” In the first part of her set, she also performed “Un Gatito Me Llamó” from her latest album Tropicoqueta as well as “QLONA” and “S91.” The next part of her set focused even more on Tropicoqueta with performances of the title track, “Papasito,” and “Ese Hombre Es Malo,” along with the billion-streams hit “MAMIII.” Half-way through she busted out “Ivonny Bonita,” “Pineapple,” and “AMARGURA” from her fourth studio album Mañana Será Bonito, a song and record that helped launched her to global stardom, and “Tu Perfume.” The latter part of her set focused on the chart material that helped her rise as force in urbano music, including “TQG” and “Bichota.” She also sang “Coleccionando Heridas” and “Si Antes te Hubiera conocido” before bringing the concert to its finale with “Viajando Por El Mundo.” The concert also featured Karol G’s latest single “Matadora,” released the same day, being played in the stadium after the live set concluded. Jamie Dimon, chairman of JPMorgan (JPM.US), expressed a markedly different view in an interview in May. He criticized the bill for allowing cryptocurrency firms to pay interest or yields on stablecoins while failing to grant them the same protective standards as traditional financial institutions. Dimon explicitly stated that such a double standard is something the banking system would never accept, arguing that it undermines the fairness of the financial system. This stance reflects the traditional banking sector's caution regarding the expansion of decentralized finance, and the fundamental divergence between the two sides over the regulatory rationale for stablecoins constitutes the primary obstacle to advancing the bill. Despite the bill's imminent vote, Republicans will need to secure support from some Democrats to reach the 60-vote threshold required for passage. Massachusetts Senator Elizabeth Warren sharply criticized the bill, pointing out that it transfers law-enforcement responsibilities to the U.S. Department of Justice rather than state authorities, and even protects the president's financial interests in the cryptocurrency sector, thereby obstructing accountability for Trump. Warren argued that the bill fails to adequately safeguard investors, the financial system, and national security, and should never have been considered for enactment in the first place. This marks another sign of legislative gridlock, following the earlier setbacks of multiple crypto‑regulation proposals. title: 50 new GS students BUILD volunteer ties across Statesboro - Statesboro Herald

For four days this week, 50 incoming Georgia Southern University first-year students who enlisted in the BUILD program divided into smaller teams and did volunteer work at various nonprofit sites, from campus to downtown Statesboro and beyond. One group of students had worked at the Statesboro Food Bank on Monday. Another team, including 10 to 15 incoming freshmen volunteers and two student “BUILD leaders” now in the junior class, showed up to work there Thursday morning – the last day of the program. They helped stock shelves with donated or otherwise newly arrived canned goods and other foodstuffs unloaded from a truck by other volunteers. One of the student leaders, Carter Ellington, 19, from Valdosta, did not go through BUILD as a freshman, but she has since participated in Southern Leaders, a multi-year student leadership program which, like BUILD, is coordinated through the university’s Office of Leadership and Community Engagement. She has also stepped forward in the community as a volunteer, such as with summer camps for foster children at 7th Mile Farm. So, Ellington was recruited to be a BUILD leader, and said she enjoyed working with the newer students and watching them grow some in just four days, or five if you count from their arrival on campus around midday Sunday. “I love volunteering and I thought I was just going to be volunteering and feeling that feeling, but actually watching them, the students, feel like they are making an impact and for one they’re being heard and seen and they’re doing something that makes other people feel heard and seen, that’s been so awesome to watch,” she said. BUILD stands for Building Undergraduate Involvement in Leadership Development, which may be one of those acronyms that led to a full name instead of the other way round. Incoming first-year students who participate arrive a full month before fall semester actually begins and pay a $200 fee to cover the cost of their lodging – in a temporary residence hall assignment – meals, transportation, equipment and leadership. The other student BUILD leader with Thursday’s group at the Food Bank, Jake Arispe, 21, from the Atlanta area, is also heading into his junior year. But BUILD leaders can be sophomores, juniors or seniors, and there were eight this year, guiding, assisting and to some extent counseling the incoming first-year student volunteers. In fact, Arispe was a BUILD volunteer the summer before his first year at Georgia Southern, and a BUILD leader going into his second year, as well as now, his third. “I had a great time my freshman year,” he said. “It definitely helped me get acclimated to campus, the community, and then also meet a bunch of different people, learned all about the community, the outreaches that different places do.” The volunteer work assignments typically last from 9 a.m. until noon. Other activities, and debriefing sessions in which volunteers and leaders talk about topics such as leadership and community involvement, occupy afternoons and evenings. The new students also get to know each other, and a little about campus and Statesboro. “I definitely felt more comfortable once I got to campus because of it,” Arispe said, recalling his freshman experience two years ago. Incidentally, Ellington is majoring in criminal justice as a pre-law student, but Arisbe majoring in sports medicine and finance. So it’s not like the student leaders are all planning to be counselors or work for some Chamber of Commerce. A variety of different academic interests was also evident in three young men, all 18 years old from various areas of Georgia, who appeared to be friends already. Miles Hill, from Austell, is an intended theater major. Tristan Clark, from Burke County, plans to major in criminal justice & criminology and to minor in cybersecurity. Myles Benjamin, from McDonough, intends on a geosciences major and hopes to become a meteorologist. Clark said the program was better than he expected when he signed up. “I think the amount of friends I’ve made this week is amazing” he said. “You know, I feel so close to them, even after just a week,” he said. One of his previous volunteer exploits of the week involved sorting shoes at a Christian ministry thrift shop. He and several of the other students said they also enjoyed some work they did at the Bulloch County Agricultural Complex. Benjamin noted that on one of the days, he had packed bags with T-shirts, grabbers and trash bags for Georgia Southern Eagles football players to use in a volunteer project of their own, cleaning up along a highway. Individual BUILD students went to four or five volunteer sites in the four work days. But altogether, the 50 freshman volunteers and eight student leaders did service work at 12 different places, reported Rachel Duvall, new this calendar year as director of the GS Office of Leadership and Community Engagement. Other jobsites included a couple of senior living facilities, Mattie Lively Elementary School, the United Way of Southeast Georgia and the university’s own Campus Community Garden. Besides getting down in the dirt gardening there, some students reported having pulled weeds and laid down mulch on the grounds of the Statesboro Family YMCA. “These incoming students really get exposed to the university and campus,” Duvall said. “So they learn some of our traditions, some of the things that make it meaningful to be a Georgia Southern Eagle, but also they are getting connected with the community. So hopefully, they’ll join us on service trips for the rest of the year.” Freshman Council within the Student Government Association is one of the opportunities some of these students may choose, she said. In addition to the SGA and Southern Leaders, the Office of Leadership and Community Engagement coordinates Serve 911, a program of weekly service trips. With those programs, students can continue to volunteer locally throughout their college years. But as a unique experience for incoming freshmen, BUILD also serves as a “little taste of independence” for some who have never been away from home before, Duvall noted. “So Day 1 they’re all nervous and they don’t want to talk to each other, and then by last (Wednesday) night they were hugging, dancing, having a party,” she said. “So it’s just nice to see them come out of their shells in a way that really prepares them for the larger college experience.” Many or all of the BUILD students will now go home before returning to campus for the real start of the semester. Operation Move-In Day is Aug. 14, for full-term classes to begin Aug. 19.
